Egress · A horizontal exit's refuge area holds both compartments: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A horizontal exit's refuge area is occupied by the same tenant or is a public area, large enough for its own occupant load plus the load expected from the adjoining compartment (the lesser of what the horizontal exit doors into it can carry and that compartment's whole load): horizontal exits aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Refuge area at 3 sq ft per occupant: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A refuge area's capacity is worked out at 3 square feet of net floor area per occupant it must hold; where the horizontal exit also forms a smoke compartment, Groups I-1, I-2 and I-3 and ambulatory care facilities meet 407.5.3, 408.6.2, 420.6.1 and 422.3.2 as they apply: refuge areas aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · A refuge area's own exits: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The refuge area a horizontal exit leads into has exits enough for its own occupants (not counting those entering through horizontal exits), at least one leading directly outside or to an interior exit stairway or ramp; but the adjoining compartment needs no stairway or door directly outside where the refuge area has them and no one must go back through the compartment they left: horizontal exits aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Standpipes at horizontal exits where 905.3 and 905.4 require: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Standpipes and standpipe hose connections are provided where 905.3 and 905.4 require them: standpipes aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Where exterior exit stairways may serve as exits: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Exterior exit stairways and ramps serving as an exit component meet 1027 (1027.1); an exterior exit stairway is not an element of a required means of egress in Group I-2, and outside Group I-2 no exterior exit stairway or ramp is one in a building more than six stories above grade plane or a high-rise building: which stairways are exterior exit stairways, and whether the building is a high-rise, aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Exterior exit stairways open on at least one side: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An exterior exit stairway or ramp serving as an element of a required means of egress is open on at least one side but for required structural columns, beams, handrails and guards, the open side having at least 35 square feet of open area at each floor level and intermediate landing, at least 42 inches above that floor or landing: exterior stairways aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Exterior exit stairways open onto yards: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The open areas beside an exterior exit stairway or ramp are yards, courts or public ways; its other sides may be enclosed by the building's exterior walls: exterior stairways and what they open onto aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Exterior exit stairways 10 ft from lot lines and other buildings: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An exterior exit stairway or ramp, landings included, has a fire separation distance of at least 10 feet, measured at right angles from its exterior edge, to adjacent lot lines, to other portions of the building (treated as separate buildings) and to other buildings on the same lot unless their exterior walls and openings are protected per 705; but at least 5 feet for one serving individual dwelling units of Group R-3: exterior stairways and their distances aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Exterior exit stairways separated from the interior: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An exterior exit stairway or ramp is separated from the interior as 1023.2 requires, with openings only those needed for egress from normally occupied spaces, and the exterior wall rated per 1023.7 where other parts of the building expose the plane of its edge at an angle under 180 degrees; but no separation is needed for occupancies other than Group R-1 or R-2 in a building of at most two stories above grade plane whose level of exit discharge is the first story above grade plane; nor where it is served by an exterior ramp or balcony connecting two remote exterior exit stairways or other approved exits, its perimeter at least 50 percent open (openings at least half the enclosing wall's height, their tops at least 7 feet above the balcony); nor from an open-ended corridor where the building is sprinklered throughout per 903.3.1.1 or 903.3.1.2, the corridors meet 1020 and connect at each end to an exterior exit stairway or ramp meeting 1027, the walls and openings beside it meet 1023.7, and each change of direction over 45 degrees has a clear opening of at least 35 square feet or an exterior stairway or ramp; nor in Group R-3 of at most four stories where it serves individual dwelling units and discharges directly to grade: exterior stairways, their separation and walls aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Exits discharge directly outside: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The exit discharge meets 1028 and 1029 and 1003 to 1015 as they apply (1028.1). Exits discharge directly to the exterior, at grade or with a direct path of egress travel to grade, never reentering a building; but at most 50 percent of the number and the minimum width or required capacity of interior exit stairways and ramps may egress through areas on the level of exit discharge (a free and unobstructed path to a readily visible exterior exit door, the whole level separated from areas below as the enclosure is, the egress path sprinklered and the portions with access to it sprinklered per 903.3.1.1 or 903.3.1.2 or separated from it, and an exit access stairway or ramp ending at least 30 feet, or a quarter of the building's greatest diagonal if less, from the exit stairway's discharge door), or through a vestibule (separated from areas below as the enclosure is, at most 10 feet deep and 30 feet long, separated from the rest of the level by a fire partition per 708, used only for egress and exiting directly outside), the two together at most 50 percent of the number and of the minimum width or required capacity of the required exits; and horizontal exits per 1026 need not discharge directly outside: where each exit discharges isn't worked out, so a person's check.

Egress · Exit discharge at least as wide as the exits it serves: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The exit discharge's minimum width or required capacity is at least that of the exits it serves: the exit discharge outside the building isn't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Exit discharge components open to the outside: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Exit discharge components are open enough to the exterior to keep smoke and toxic gases from building up: the exit discharge isn't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Exit discharge reaches a public way: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The exit discharge gives direct and unobstructed access to a public way; where that can't be provided, a safe dispersal area of at least 5 square feet per person, on the same lot at least 50 feet from the building, permanently kept and identified as one, with a safe and unobstructed path from the building: the site outside the building isn't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Egress courts at least 44 in wide: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An egress court serving as an exit discharge component meets 1029 (1029.1): its capacity is as 1005.1 requires and its width at least 44 inches, or 36 inches serving Groups R-3 and U, and never less than the required capacity, the width and capacity unobstructed to a height of 7 feet but for encroachments complying with 1005.7: egress courts aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Narrow egress courts' walls rated 1 hour: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where an egress court is less than 10 feet wide, its walls are rated at least 1 hour for 10 feet above its floor, openings in them protected at least 3/4 hour; but not for an egress court serving fewer than 10 occupants, one serving Group R-3, or one at grade giving direct and unobstructed access to a public way by two or more independent paths, each keeping the required width or capacity, whichever is greater: egress courts and their walls aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Bleachers and grandstands per ICC 300: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Bleachers, grandstands and folding and telescopic seating that are not building elements comply with ICC 300: such seating isn't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Spaces under grandstands separated by 1-hour construction: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Spaces under grandstands or bleachers are separated by fire barriers per 707 and horizontal assemblies per 711 of at least 1-hour fire-resistance-rated construction; but not ticket booths under 100 square feet, toilet rooms, or other accessory use areas of 1,000 square feet or less sprinklered per 903.3.1.1: grandstands, bleachers and the spaces under them aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · An assembly main exit for at least half the occupants: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A building, room or space used for assembly purposes with an occupant load over 300 and a main exit: the main exit has capacity for at least half the occupant load, and at least the total required capacity of all the means of egress leading to it; where the building is classified Group A, the main exit fronts at least one street, or an unoccupied space at least 10 feet wide adjoining a street or public way; where there is no well-defined main exit, or there are several, the exits may be distributed around the building's perimeter if their total capacity is at least 100 percent of the required capacity: which exit is the main exit, and its capacity, aren't worked out, so a person's check.

Egress · Assembly other exits for at least half of each level's occupants: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Each level of a building used for assembly purposes with an occupant load over 300 and a main exit has, besides access to the main exit, more means of egress with capacity for at least half the total occupant load that level serves, complying with 1007.1; where there is no well-defined main exit, or there are several, each level's exits may be distributed around the building's perimeter if their total width is at least 100 percent of the required width: the main exit and the other exits' share aren't worked out, so a person's check.

Egress · Waiting lobbies in Group A-1 kept out of the egress width: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): In Group A-1, where people are let in while no seats are free, they may wait in a lobby or similar space that doesn't encroach on the minimum width or required capacity of the means of egress; such a foyer, unless every main entrance or exit connects it directly to a public street, has a straight and unobstructed corridor or path of travel to each of them: waiting spaces aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Two exits from balconies and galleries seating 50 or more: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A balcony, gallery or press box seating 50 or more in a building, room or space used for assembly purposes has at least two means of egress, one from each side: balconies, galleries and press boxes aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Assembly aisle capacity without smoke protection: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Aisles serving assembly seating have at least the capacity 1030.6.1 sets where the seating isn't smoke-protected (1030.6.2 sets it where it is, 1030.6.3 where it is open-air): at least 0.3 inch per occupant served on stepped aisles with risers of 7 inches or less and treads of 11 inches or more; at least 0.005 inch more per occupant for each 0.10 inch of riser above 7 inches; at least 0.075 inch more per occupant on the parts of a stepped aisle descent with no handrail within 30 inches horizontally; at least 0.22 inch per occupant on ramped aisles steeper than 1 in 12, and 0.20 inch on level aisles and ramped aisles not that steep: aisles and the occupants they serve aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Aisle capacity for smoke-protected assembly seating: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An aisle for smoke-protected assembly seating has capacity of at least the occupant load it serves times Table 1030.6.2's factor for the total number of seats exposed to the same smoke-protected environment (interpolation between its values permitted), and a facility using the table's reduced widths has a life safety evaluation per NFPA 101: whether seating is smoke-protected, and its aisles, aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Smoke-protected aisle capacity per seat: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Inches of aisle capacity per seat served in smoke-protected assembly seating, by the total number of seats in it: at 5,000 or fewer, 0.200 on stepped aisles with handrails within 30 inches, 0.250 on stepped aisles without, 0.150 on level aisles or ramped aisles not steeper than 1 in 10, and 0.165 on ramped aisles steeper than 1 in 10; at 10,000, 0.130, 0.163, 0.100 and 0.110; at 15,000, 0.096, 0.120, 0.070 and 0.077; at 20,000, 0.076, 0.095, 0.056 and 0.062; at 25,000 or more, 0.060, 0.075, 0.044 and 0.048: aisles and their seats aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Smoke control for smoke-protected assembly seating: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Aisles and aisle accessways serving smoke-protected assembly seating have a smoke control system per 909, or natural ventilation designed to keep the smoke level at least 6 feet above the floor of the means of egress: smoke control isn't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · A roof at least 15 ft above the highest aisle: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where smoke-protected assembly seating has a roof, the lowest portion of the roof deck is at least 15 feet above the highest aisle or aisle accessway; but an outdoor stadium's roof canopy may be lower where nothing is less than 80 inches above the highest aisle or aisle accessway: roofs over seating aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Sprinklers where there is smoke-protected seating: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Enclosed areas with walls and ceilings in buildings or structures with smoke-protected assembly seating are protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system per 903.3.1.1; but not the floor area used for contests, performances or entertainment where the roof construction is more than 50 feet above the floor and the use is restricted to low fire hazard uses, nor press boxes and storage facilities under 1,000 square feet: whether seating is smoke-protected isn't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Aisle capacity for open-air assembly seating: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): In open-air assembly seating, an aisle has capacity of at least the total occupant load it serves times 0.08 inch where egress is by stepped aisle, and 0.06 inch where it is by level or ramped aisles; or 1030.6.2's capacity for the number of seats where that is less: whether seating is open-air, and its aisles, aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Sprinklers where there is open-air seating: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Enclosed areas with walls and ceilings in buildings or structures with open-air assembly seating are protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system per 903.3.1.1; but not the floor area used for contests, performances or entertainment where the roof construction is more than 50 feet above the floor and the use is restricted to low fire hazard uses, press boxes and storage facilities under 1,000 square feet, or open-air seating facilities whose seating and means of egress in the seating area are essentially open to the outside: whether seating is open-air isn't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · A path through an adjacent row: at most 24 seats between aisles: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where one of the two paths of travel crosses the aisle through a row of seats to another aisle, there are at most 24 seats between the two aisles, and the row between them is at least 12 inches clear plus 0.6 inch for each seat above seven; for smoke-protected or open-air seating, at most 40 seats, and 12 inches plus 0.3 inch for each additional seat: seats and rows aren't drawn, so a person's check.

Egress · Aisles to the exits from every occupied part of an assembly space: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Every occupied portion of a building, room or space used for assembly purposes that contains seats, tables, displays, similar fixtures or equipment has aisles leading to exits or exit access doorways as 1030 requires (1030.1: a room or space used for assembly purposes containing seats, tables, displays, equipment or other material complies with 1030): aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Assembly aisles' least clear widths: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An aisle's clear width is at least: 48 inches for stepped aisles with seating on both sides, or 36 inches where they serve fewer than 50 seats; 36 inches for stepped aisles with seating on one side only, or 23 inches between a stepped aisle handrail and the seating where the aisle serves no more than five rows on one side; 23 inches between a stepped aisle handrail or guard and the seating where a mid-aisle handrail divides the stepped aisle; 42 inches for level or ramped aisles with seating on both sides, or 36 inches where they serve fewer than 50 seats, or 30 inches where they serve fewer than 15 seats and aren't part of an accessible route; 36 inches for level or ramped aisles with seating on one side only, or 30 inches where they serve fewer than 15 seats and aren't part of an accessible route: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Aisle capacity for its catchment area: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An aisle has capacity enough for the people in the catchment area it serves, the portion of the whole space that section of the aisle serves, worked out assuming a balanced use of all the means of egress, the number of people in proportion to egress capacity: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Converging aisles' combined capacity: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where aisles converge into a single path of egress travel, that path's required capacity is at least the combined required capacity of the converging aisles: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Uniform aisle width where egress may go either way: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The portions of aisles where egress is possible in either of two directions are uniform in minimum width or required capacity: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Dead-end assembly aisles: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Each end of an aisle continues to a cross aisle, foyer, doorway, vomitory, concourse or stairway per 1030.9.7 with access to an exit; but a dead-end aisle may be up to 20 feet long; longer where the seats beyond its first 20 feet are at most 24 seats from another aisle, along a row at least 12 inches clear plus 0.6 inch for each seat above seven where the seats have backrests, or beyond 10 where they don't; one serving fewer than 50 seats and complying with 1030.8; and for smoke-protected or open-air seating, dead-end vertical aisles of 21 rows or fewer, or longer where the rows beyond are at most 40 seats from another aisle, along an aisle accessway at least 12 inches clear plus 0.3 inch for each seat above seven where the seats have backrests, or beyond 10 where they don't: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Aisle width measured to walls: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An aisle's clear width is measured to walls, edges of seating and tread edges, but for permitted projections; an aisle beside seating at tables may be measured per 1030.13.1 instead: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · No obstructions in assembly aisles: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Nothing obstructs an aisle's minimum width or required capacity; but handrails may project into the required width of stepped and ramped aisles per 1014.9: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Stairways from stepped aisles to cross aisles or concourses: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A stairway connecting a stepped aisle to a cross aisle or concourse may meet 1030.14's assembly aisle walking surface requirements, and the transitions between such stairways and stepped aisles comply with 1030.10: stepped aisles and their stairways aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Stairways from vomitories to cross aisles or concourses: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A stairway connecting a vomitory to a cross aisle or concourse may meet 1030.14's assembly aisle walking surface requirements, and the transitions between such stairways and stepped aisles comply with 1030.10: vomitories and their stairways aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Stairs that keep a stepped aisle's risers and treads: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A transition between a stairway and a stepped aisle meets 1030.10.1 or 1030.10.2: where the stepped aisles, transitions and stairways keep the stepped aisle's riser and tread dimensions, they comply with 1030.14 as one exit access component: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Straight-run transitions at least 22 or 30 in deep: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where a stairway and a stepped aisle with different riser and tread dimensions meet (1030.10.2 to 1030.10.3) in a straight run, the transition is at least 22 inches deep where the treads on its descending side are deeper, or at least 30 inches where they are shallower: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Transitions where a stairway turns from a stepped aisle: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where the stairway changes direction from the stepped aisle, the transition between them is at least 11 inches deep, or the stepped aisle's tread depth if that is more: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · A 1 to 2 in marking stripe at each transition: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A distinctive marking stripe at least 1 inch and at most 2 inches wide is at each nosing or leading edge next to the transition, distinctly different from the stepped aisle's contrasting marking stripe: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Stepped aisle treads turning at a vomitory: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where a stepped aisle changes direction at a vomitory (1030.11), its treads there are at least 11 inches deep, or the stepped aisle's tread depth if that is more, and a tread's height above a transition at a vomitory complies with 1030.14.2.2: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Transitions at the top of a vomitory: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A transition between the stepped aisle above a vomitory and the stepped aisles beside it is at least 11 inches deep, or the stepped aisle's tread depth if that is more: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Aisles built of materials the construction type allows: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Aisles, stepped aisles and ramped aisles are built of materials consistent with the types permitted for the building's type of construction; wood handrails are permitted in every type: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Slip-resistant aisle surfaces: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The surface of aisles, stepped aisles and ramped aisles is of slip-resistant materials, securely attached, and a stepped aisle's surface complies with 1011.7.1: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Outdoor aisles shed water: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Outdoor aisles, stepped aisles and ramped aisles, and the outdoor approaches to them, are designed so that water doesn't accumulate on the walking surface: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Aisle width at tables measured 19 in from the table edge: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Aisle accessways serve seating at tables per 1030.13.1 and seating in rows per 1030.13.2: where seating at a table or counter is next to an aisle or aisle accessway, its required clear width is measured to a line 19 inches from and parallel to the table's or counter's edge, measured perpendicular to that side; other side boundaries are measured to walls, edges of seating and tread edges; where fixed seats serve the tables or counters, the width is measured from the back of the seat: tables and seats aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Table aisle accessways: 12 in plus 1/2 in a foot past 12 ft: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An aisle accessway serving seating at tables or counters meets 1005.1's capacity and is at least 12 inches wide plus 1/2 inch for each additional foot, or part of one, beyond 12 feet of its length measured from the center of the seat farthest from an aisle; but a portion at most 6 feet long and used by at most four people in all is exempt: tables and seats aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Table aisle accessways at most 30 ft to two paths: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Travel along an aisle accessway at tables is at most 30 feet from any seat to the point where a person has a choice of two or more paths of egress travel to separate exits: tables and seats aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Rows of 14 or fewer seats at least 12 in apart: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where rows have 14 or fewer seats, the aisle accessway between them is at least 12 inches clear, measured horizontally from the back of the row ahead to the nearest projection of the row behind: with automatic or self-rising seats raised, any other seat down, and folding tablet arms in use (or stored, where a tablet arm raised to vertical in one motion falls back to stored by gravity): seats and rows aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Rows reached at both ends: at most 100 seats: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A row of seating served by aisles or doorways at both ends has at most 100 seats, and the 12 inches between rows grows by 0.3 inch for every seat beyond 14 where the seats have backrests, or beyond 21 where they don't, to at most 22 inches needed; for smoke-protected or open-air seating, Table 1030.13.2.1 gives the row lengths a 12-inch aisle accessway may serve before it widens: seats and rows aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Smoke-protected rows' seats with 12 in between: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The most seats a row of smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating may have with a 12-inch clear aisle accessway, by the total number of seats (with backrests and without, an aisle or doorway at both ends, then at one end only): fewer than 4,000, 14, 21, 7 and 10; 4,000 to 6,999, 15, 22, 7 and 10; 7,000 to 9,999, 16, 23, 8 and 11; 10,000 to 12,999, 17, 24, 8 and 11; 13,000 to 15,999, 18, 25, 9 and 12; 16,000 to 18,999, 19, 26, 9 and 12; 19,000 to 21,999, 20, 27, 10 and 13; 22,000 and more, 21, 28, 11 and 14: seats and rows aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Rows reached at one end: 12 in plus 0.6 in a seat: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): For a row served by an aisle or doorway at one end only, the 12 inches between rows grows by 0.6 inch for every seat beyond seven where the seats have backrests, or beyond 10 where they don't, to at most 22 inches needed; for smoke-protected or open-air seating, Table 1030.13.2.1 gives the row lengths a 12-inch aisle accessway may serve before it widens: seats and rows aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Ramped aisles at most 1 in 8: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Ramped aisles comply with 1030.14.1 to 1030.14.1.3 and stepped aisles with 1030.14.2 to 1030.14.2.4: an aisle sloped more than 1 in 20 (5 percent) is a ramped aisle; one that is part of an accessible route per 1009 and 1109.2 is at most 1 in 12 (8 percent), and any other at most 1 in 8 (12.5 percent): aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · A ramped aisle's cross slope at most 1 in 48: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A ramped aisle's slope measured perpendicular to the direction of travel is not steeper than 1 in 48 (2 percent): aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Landings for ramped aisles per 1012.6: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Ramped aisles have landings per 1012.6 to 1012.6.5, which may overlap required aisles or cross aisles: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Edge protection for ramped aisles per 1012.10: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Ramped aisles have edge protection per 1012.10 and 1012.10.1; but in assembly spaces with fixed seating, not on the sides where the ramped aisle gives access to the adjacent seating and aisle accessways: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Aisles steeper than 1 in 8 are stepped aisles: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An aisle sloped more than 1 in 8 (12.5 percent) is a series of risers and treads across its full width, complying with 1030.14.2.1 to 1030.14.2.4: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Stepped aisle treads at least 11 in: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Stepped aisle treads are at least 11 inches deep and uniform, adjacent treads differing by at most 3/16 inch: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Stepped aisle risers 4 to 8 in: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where a stepped aisle's gradient matches the adjoining seating's, its risers are at least 4 and at most 8 inches high and uniform within each flight; but they may vary only as far as the seating's changing gradient needs for sightlines, each variation over 3/16 inch between adjacent risers marked by a distinctive stripe 1 to 2 inches wide on each tread at the nosing next to it, distinct from the contrasting marking stripe; and risers up to 9 inches are permitted where the adjacent seating's slope needs them for sightlines: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Stepped aisle riser tolerances: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Adjacent risers designed equal differ by at most 3/16 inch; where the stepped aisle takes 1030.14.2.2's exception 1, each riser of unequal height differs from the adjacent ones, in the direction of descent, by at most 3/8 inch where its treads are less than 22 inches deep, and by at most 3/4 inch where they are 22 inches or more: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · A 1 to 2 in contrasting stripe on each tread: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Each tread has a contrasting marking stripe at least 1 inch and at most 2 inches wide at its nosing or leading edge, so each tread is readily seen in descent; but it may be left out where the tread surfaces already make each tread readily apparent in descent: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Stepped aisle nosings per 1011.5.5: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A stepped aisle's nosing and riser profile comply with 1011.5.5 to 1011.5.5.3: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Assembly seats fastened to the floor: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): In a building, room or space used for assembly purposes, seats are securely fastened to the floor; but not where there are no ramped or tiered floors for seating and 200 or fewer seats, nor at tables without ramped or tiered floors; over 200 seats without ramped or tiered floors, they are fastened together in groups of at least three or fastened to the floor; where flexible seating is integral to a space on tiered levels, up to 200 seats need not be fastened (plans showing seating, tiers and aisles submitted for approval); nor groups of at most 14 seats on level floors set apart by railings, guards, partial height walls or similar barriers; nor seats for musicians or other performers set apart so: seats aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Handrails on stepped aisles and steep ramped aisles: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Ramped aisles sloped more than 1 in 15 (6.7 percent) and stepped aisles have handrails per 1014, at one or both sides or within the aisle width; a stepped aisle with seating on one side and 74 inches wide or more has two, one within 30 inches horizontally of the side of the tiered floor next to it; but no handrails are needed on ramped aisles with seating on both sides, nor where a guard at the aisle's side has a top as graspable as a handrail per 1014.4, and no extensions at the top and bottom where they would block crossovers: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Mid-aisle handrails broken every five rows or fewer: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where there is seating on both sides of the aisle, or a stepped aisle needs two handrails, mid-aisle handrails are discontinuous, with gaps or breaks at most every five rows, each at least 22 and at most 36 inches clear, measured horizontally, and the handrail ends rounded or bent: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Side handrails return or continue: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Handrails at the side of stepped aisles return to a wall, guard or the walking surface, or continue to the handrail of the next stepped aisle flight: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Mid-aisle handrails end within 18 in of the lowest riser: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Mid-aisle handrails don't extend beyond the lowest riser and end within 18 inches of it, measured horizontally, with no extensions needed; but they may extend beyond it where their extensions don't obstruct the cross aisle's width: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · A rail about 12 in below mid-aisle handrails: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where stepped aisles have mid-aisle handrails, an additional rail is about 12 inches below the handrail, its strength and attachment per 1607.9.1.2: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Guards beside assembly seating per 1015: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Guards next to seating in a building, room or space used for assembly purposes are provided where 1015 requires them and built per 1015, except as 1030.17.1 to 1030.17.4 provide; at bleachers, grandstands and folding and telescopic seating, guards are provided where ICC 300 and 1030.17.1 require them: guards and seating aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Perimeter guards where seating is over 30 in up: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Perimeter guards are provided where the footboards or walking surface of seating are more than 30 inches above the floor or grade below: at least 42 inches high measured from the seatboard where seatboards adjoin the perimeter, or from the floor where seats are self-rising, and measured per 1015.3 where an aisle lies between the seating and the perimeter; but guards that impact sightlines may meet 1030.17.3, and bleachers, grandstands and folding and telescopic seating need none where the seating is next to a wall less than 4 inches away: guards and seating aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Cross aisle guards: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Cross aisles more than 30 inches above the floor or grade below have guards per 1015; where the drop between a cross aisle and the floor or grade below is 30 inches or less, guards at least 26 inches above the aisle floor; but none where the backs of the seats at the front of the cross aisle rise 24 inches or more above the aisle's floor: guards and cross aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Guards that would block sightlines at least 26 in: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Unless 1030.17.4 applies, a fascia or railing system meeting 1015's guard requirements and at least 26 inches high is provided where the floor or footboard is more than 30 inches above the floor or grade below and the fascia or railing would otherwise interfere with the sightlines of the seating right beside it: guards and seating aren't in the model, so a person's check.

Egress · Guards at the foot of aisles at least 36 in high: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where the foot of an aisle is more than 30 inches above the floor or grade below, a fascia or railing system meeting 1015's guard requirements runs the aisle's full width, at least 36 inches high and giving at least 42 inches measured diagonally between the top of the rail and the nosing of the nearest tread: guards and aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

definitions.text: HEIGHT OF BUILDING — he vertical distance measured from grade plane to the highest level of a flat or mansard roof or to the average height of a pitched, gabled, hip or gambrel roof, excluding bulkheads, housing for mechanical equipment, towers and similar constructions not intended for human occupancy or necessary equipment carried above roof level. Where a building contains sections of a roof of varying heights, the height of that building shall be measured using that section of the roof that has the highest elevation from grade plane.

GRADE PLANE — A reference plane representing the average of finished ground level on each side of the building at exterior walls. On the sides of the building where grade is level, the measurement will be taken at a point adjoining the building. Where the finished ground level slopes away from the exterior walls, the measurement shall be taken at the lowest point within the area between the building and the lot line or, where the lot line is more than six feet from the building, between the building and a point six feet from the building.

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).

quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).
quotes.where: 1030.8, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.355
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1018.4 Aisle accessways in Group M. An aisle accessway shall be provided on not less than one side of each element within the merchandise pad. The minimum clear width for an aisle accessway not required to be accessible shall be 30 inches (762 mm). The required clear width of the aisle accessway shall be measured perpendicular to the elements and merchandise within the merchan- dise pad. The 30-inch (762 mm) minimum clear width shall be maintained to provide a path to an adjacent aisle or aisle accessway. The common path of egress travel shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any point in the merchandise pad. Exception: For areas serving not more than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm).

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).
quotes.where: 1030.8, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.355
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1018.4 Aisle accessways in Group M. An aisle accessway shall be provided on not less than one side of each element within the merchandise pad. The minimum clear width for an aisle accessway not required to be accessible shall be 30 inches (762 mm). The required clear width of the aisle accessway shall be measured perpendicular to the elements and merchandise within the merchan- dise pad. The 30-inch (762 mm) minimum clear width shall be maintained to provide a path to an adjacent aisle or aisle accessway. The common path of egress travel shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any point in the merchandise pad. Exception: For areas serving not more than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm).
quotes.where: 1018.4, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.342
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).
quotes.where: 1030.8, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.355
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
