quotes.text: 1008.2.1 Illumination level under normal power. The means of egress illumination level shall be not less than 1 footcandle (11 lux) at the walking surface. Along exit access stairways, exit stairways and at their required landings, the illumination level shall not be less than 10 footcandles (108 lux) at the walking surface when the stairway is in use. Exception: For auditoriums, theaters, concert or opera halls and similar assembly occupancies, the illumination at the walking surface is permitted to be reduced during performances by one of the following methods provided that the required illumina- tion is automatically restored upon activation of a premises’ fire alarm system: 1. Externally illuminated walking surfaces shall be permitted to be illuminated to not less than 0.2 footcandle (2.15 lux). 2. Steps, landings and the sides of ramps shall be permitted to be marked with self-luminous materials in accordance with Sections 1025.2.1, 1025.2.2 and 1025.2.4 by systems listed in accordance with UL 1994.

quotes.text: 1013.1 Where required. Exits and exit access doors shall be marked by an approved exit sign readily visible from any direction of egress travel. The path of egress travel to exits and within exits shall be marked by readily visible exit signs to clearly indicate the direction of egress travel in cases where the exit or the path of egress travel is not immediately visible to the occupants. quotes.text: 1009.7.2 Separation. Exterior walls separating the exterior area of assisted rescue from the interior of the building shall have a minimum fire-resistance rating of 1 hour, rated for exposure to fire from the inside. The fire-resistance-rated exterior wall construction shall extend horizontally not less than 10 feet (3048 mm) beyond the landing on either side of the landing or equiva- lent fire-resistance-rated construction is permitted to extend out perpendicular to the exterior wall not less than 4 feet (1219 mm) on the side of the landing. The fire-resistance-rated construction shall extend vertically from the ground to a point not less than 10 feet (3048 mm) above the floor level of the area for assisted rescue or to the roof line, whichever is lower. Openings within such fire-resistance-rated exterior walls shall be protected in accordance with Section 716. Exception: The fire-resistance rating and opening protectives are not required in the exterior wall where the building is equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1 or 903.3.1.2.

Exceptions: 1. Exit access stairways and ramps within a two-story opening complying with Section 712.1.9. 2. Exit access stairways serving and contained within a Group R-3 congregate residence or a Group R-4 facility are not required to be enclosed. 4. Exit access stairways and ramps in buildings equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1, where the area of the vertical opening between stories does not exceed twice the horizontal projected area of the stairway or ramp and the opening is protected by a draft curtain and closely spaced sprinklers in accordance with NFPA 13. In other than Group B and M occupancies, this provision is limited to openings that do not connect more than four stories. 5. Exit access stairways and ramps within an atrium complying with the provisions of Section 404. 6. Exit access stairways and ramps in open parking garages that serve only the parking garage. 7. Exit access stairways and ramps serving smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating complying with the exit access travel distance requirements of Section 1030.7. 8. Exit access stairways and ramps between the balcony, gallery or press box and the main assembly floor in occupancies such as theaters, places of religious worship, auditoriums and sports facilities. 9. Exterior exit access stairways or ramps between occupiable roofs.

quotes.text: 1023.3.1 Extension. Where interior exit stairways and ramps are extended to an exit discharge or a public way by an exit passage- way, the interior exit stairway and ramp shall be separated from the exit passageway by a fire barrier constructed in accordance with Section 707 or a horizontal assembly constructed in accordance with Section 711, or both. The fire-resistance rating shall be not less than that required for the interior exit stairway and ramp. A fire door assembly complying with Section 716 shall be installed in the fire barrier to provide a means of egress from the interior exit stairway and ramp to the exit passageway. Openings in the fire barrier other than the fire door assembly are prohibited. Penetrations of the fire barrier are prohibited. Exceptions: 1. Penetrations of the fire barrier in accordance with Section 1023.5 shall be permitted. 2. Separation between an interior exit stairway or ramp and the exit passageway extension shall not be required where there are no openings into the exit passageway extension. 3. Separation between an interior exit stairway or ramp and the exit passageway extension shall not be required where the interior exit stairway and the exit passageway extension are pressurized in accordance with Section 909.20.4.

quotes.text: 1023.6 Ventilation. Equipment and ductwork for interior exit stairway and ramp ventilation as permitted by Section 1023.5 shall comply with one of the following items: 1. Such equipment and ductwork shall be located exterior to the building and shall be directly connected to the interior exit stairway and ramp by ductwork enclosed in construction as required for shafts. 2. quotes.text: 1025.2.4.2 Wall-mounted demarcation lines. Perimeter demarcation lines shall be placed on the wall with the bottom edge of the stripe not more than 4 inches (102 mm) above the finished floor. At the top or bottom of the stairs, demarcation lines shall drop vertically to the floor within 2 inches (51 mm) of the step or landing edge. Demarcation lines on walls shall transition vertically to the floor and then extend across the floor where a line on the floor is the only practical method of outlining the path. Where the wall line is broken by a door, demarcation lines on walls shall continue across the face of the door or transition to the floor and extend across the floor in front of such door. Exception: Demarcation lines shall not extend in front of exit discharge doors that lead out of an exit and through which occupants must travel to complete the exit path.

quotes.text: 1026.1 General. Horizontal exits serving as an exit in a means of egress system shall comply with the requirements of this section. Exceptions: 1. Horizontal exits are permitted to comprise two-thirds of the required exits from any building or floor area for occupancies in Group I-2. 2. Horizontal exits are permitted to comprise 100 percent of the exits required for occupancies in Group I-3. Not less than 6 square feet (0.6 m2) of accessible space per occupant shall be provided on each side of the horizontal exit for the total number of people in adjoining compartments.

quotes.text: 1026.2 Separation. The separation between buildings or refuge areas connected by a horizontal exit shall be provided by a fire wall complying with Section 706; or by a fire barrier complying with Section 707 or a horizontal assembly complying with Section 711, or both. The minimum fire-resistance rating of the separation shall be 2 hours. Opening protectives in horizontal exits shall also comply with Section 716. Duct and air transfer openings in a fire wall or fire barrier that serves as a horizontal exit shall also comply with Section 717. The horizontal exit separation shall extend vertically through all levels of the building unless floor assemblies have a fire- resistance rating of not less than 2 hours and do not have unprotected openings. Exception: A fire-resistance rating is not required at horizontal exits between a building area and an above-grade pedestrian walk- way constructed in accordance with Section 3104, provided that the distance between connected buildings is more than 20 feet (6096 mm). quotes.text: 1027.6 Exterior exit stairway and ramp protection. Exterior exit stairways and ramps shall be separated from the interior of the building as required in Section 1023.2. Openings shall be limited to those necessary for egress from normally occupied spaces. Where a vertical plane projecting from the edge of an exterior exit stairway or ramp and landings is exposed by other parts of the building at an angle of less than 180 degrees (3.14 rad), the exterior wall shall be rated in accordance with Section 1023.7. Exceptions: 1. Separation from the interior of the building is not required for occupancies, other than those in Group R-1 or R-2, in build- ings that are not more than two stories above grade plane where a level of exit discharge serving such occupancies is the first story above grade plane. 2. Separation from the interior of the building is not required where the exterior exit stairway or ramp is served by an exte- rior exit ramp or balcony that connects two remote exterior exit stairways or other approved exits with a perimeter that is not less than 50 percent open. To be considered open, the opening shall be not less than 50 percent of the height of the enclosing wall, with the top of the openings not less than 7 feet (2134 mm) above the top of the balcony. 3. Separation from the open-ended corridor of the building is not required for exterior exit stairways or ramps, provided that Items 3.1 through 3.5 are met: 3.1. The building, including open-ended corridors, and stairways and ramps, shall be equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1 or 903.3.1.2. 3.2. The open-ended corridors comply with Section 1020. 3.3. The open-ended corridors are connected on each end to an exterior exit stairway or ramp complying with Section 1027. 3.4. The exterior walls and openings adjacent to the exterior exit stairway or ramp comply with Section 1023.7. 3.5. At any location in an open-ended corridor where a change of direction exceeding 45 degrees (0.79 rad) occurs, a clear opening of not less than 35 square feet (3.3 m[fn2]) or an exterior stairway or ramp shall be provided. Where clear openings are provided, they shall be located so as to minimize the accumulation of smoke or toxic gases. 4. In Group R-3 occupancies not more than four stories in height, exterior exit stairways and ramps serving individual dwell- ing units are not required to be separated from the interior of the building where the exterior exit stairway or ramp discharges directly to grade.

quotes.text: 1028.2 Exit discharge. Exits shall discharge directly to the exterior of the building. The exit discharge shall be at grade or shall provide a direct path of egress travel to grade. The exit discharge shall not reenter a building. The combined use of Exceptions 1 and 2 shall not exceed 50 percent of the number and minimum width or required capacity of the required exits. Exceptions: 1. Not more than 50 percent of the number and minimum width or required capacity of interior exit stairways and ramps is permitted to egress through areas, including atriums, on the level of discharge provided that all of the following condi- tions are met: 1.1. Discharge of interior exit stairways and ramps shall be provided with a free and unobstructed path of travel to an exterior exit door and such exit is readily visible and identifiable from the point of termination of the enclosure. 1.2. The entire area of the level of exit discharge is separated from areas below by construction conforming to the fire-resistance rating for the enclosure. 1.3. The egress path from the interior exit stairway and ramp on the level of exit discharge is protected throughout by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Portions of the level of exit discharge with access to the egress path shall be either equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1 or 903.3.1.2, or separated from the egress path in accordance with the requirements for the enclosure of interior exit stairways or ramps. 1.4. Where a required interior exit stairway or ramp and an exit access stairway or ramp serve the same floor level and terminate at the same level of exit discharge, the termination of the exit access stairway or ramp and the exit discharge door of the interior exit stairway or ramp shall be separated by a distance of not less than 30 feet (9144 mm) or not less than one-fourth the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the building, which- ever is less. The distance shall be measured in a straight line between the exit discharge door from the interior exit stairway or ramp and the last tread of the exit access stairway or termination of slope of the exit access ramp. 2. Not more than 50 percent of the number and minimum width or required capacity of the interior exit stairways and ramps is permitted to egress through a vestibule provided that all of the following conditions are met: 2.1. The entire area of the vestibule is separated from areas below by construction conforming to the fire-resistance rating of the interior exit stairway or ramp enclosure. 2.2. The depth from the exterior of the building is not greater than 10 feet (3048 mm) and the length is not greater than 30 feet (9144 mm). 2.3. The area is separated from the remainder of the level of exit discharge by a fire partition constructed in accor- dance with Section 708. Exception: The maximum transmitted temperature rise is not required. 2.4. The area is used only for means of egress and exits directly to the outside. 3. Horizontal exits complying with Section 1026 shall not be required to discharge directly to the exterior of the building.

quotes.text: 1029.2 Width or capacity. The required capacity of egress courts shall be determined as specified in Section 1005.1, but the mini- mum width shall be not less than 44 inches (1118 mm), except as specified herein. quotes.text: 1030.2 Assembly main exit. A building, room or space used for assembly purposes that has an occupant load of greater than 300 and is provided with a main exit, that main exit shall be of sufficient capacity to accommodate not less than one-half of the occupant load, but such capacity shall be not less than the total required capacity of all means of egress leading to the exit. Where the building is classified as a Group A occupancy, the main exit shall front on not less than one street or an unoccupied space of not less than 10 feet (3048 mm) in width that adjoins a street or public way. In a building, room or space used for assembly purposes where there is not a well-defined main exit or where multiple main exits are provided, exits shall be permitted to be distributed around the perime- ter of the building provided that the total capacity of egress is not less than 100 percent of the required capacity.

quotes.text: 1030.13.1 Seating at tables. Where seating is located at a table or counter and is adjacent to an aisle or aisle accessway, the measurement of required clear width of the aisle or aisle accessway shall be made to a line 19 inches (483 mm) away from and parallel to the edge of the table or counter. The 19-inch (483 mm) distance shall be measured perpendicular to the side of the table or counter. In the case of other side boundaries for aisles or aisle accessways, the clear width shall be measured to walls, edges of seating and tread edges. Exception: Where tables or counters are served by fixed seats, the width of the aisle or aisle accessway shall be measured from the back of the seat.

quotes.text: 1030.13.2 Clear width of aisle accessways serving seating in rows. Where seating rows have 14 or fewer seats, the minimum clear aisle accessway width shall be not less than 12 inches (305 mm) measured as the clear horizontal distance from the back of the row ahead and the nearest projection of the row behind. Where chairs have automatic or self-rising seats, the measurement shall be made with seats in the raised position. Where any chair in the row does not have an automatic or self-rising seat, the measurements shall be made with the seat in the down position. For seats with folding tablet arms, row spacing shall be deter- mined with the tablet arm in the used position. Exception: For seats with folding tablet arms, row spacing is permitted to be determined with the tablet arm in the stored position where the tablet arm when raised manually to vertical position in one motion automatically returns to the stored position by force of gravity.

quotes.text: 1030.14.2.2 Risers. Where the gradient of stepped aisles is to be the same as the gradient of adjoining seating areas, the riser height shall be not less than 4 inches (102 mm) nor more than 8 inches (203 mm) and shall be uniform within each flight. Exceptions: 1. Riser height nonuniformity shall be limited to the extent necessitated by changes in the gradient of the adjoining seating area to maintain adequate sightlines. Where nonuniformities exceed 3/16 inch (4.8 mm) between adjacent risers, the exact location of such nonuniformities shall be indicated with a distinctive marking stripe on each tread at the nosing or leading edge adjacent to the nonuniform risers. Riser heights not exceeding 9 inches (229 mm) shall be permitted where they are necessitated by the slope of the adjacent seating areas to maintain sightlines.

quotes.text: 1030.15 Seat stability. In a building, room or space used for assembly purposes, the seats shall be securely fastened to the floor. Exceptions: 1. In a building, room or space used for assembly purposes or portions thereof without ramped or tiered floors for seating and with 200 or fewer seats, the seats shall not be required to be fastened to the floor. 2. In a building, room or space used for assembly purposes or portions thereof with seating at tables and without ramped or tiered floors for seating, the seats shall not be required to be fastened to the floor. 3. In a building, room or space used for assembly purposes or portions thereof without ramped or tiered floors for seating and with greater than 200 seats, the seats shall be fastened together in groups of not less than three or the seats shall be securely fastened to the floor. 4. In a building, room or space used for assembly purposes where flexibility of the seating arrangement is an integral part of the design and function of the space and seating is on tiered levels, not more than 200 seats shall not be required to be fastened to the floor. Plans showing seating, tiers and aisles shall be submitted for approval. 5. Groups of seats within a building, room or space used for assembly purposes separated from other seating by railings, guards, partial height walls or similar barriers with level floors and having not more than 14 seats per group shall not be required to be fastened to the floor. 6. Seats intended for musicians or other performers and separated by railings, guards, partial height walls or similar barri- ers shall not be required to be fastened to the floor.

quotes.text: 1030.16 Handrails. Ramped aisles having a slope exceeding one unit vertical in 15 units horizontal (6.7-percent slope) and stepped aisles shall be provided with handrails in compliance with Section 1014 located either at one or both sides of the aisle or within the aisle width. Where stepped aisles have seating on one side and the aisle width is 74 inches (1880 mm) or greater, two handrails are required. Where two handrails are required, one of the handrails shall be within 30 inches (762 mm) horizontally of the side of the tiered floor adjacent to the stepped aisle. Exceptions: 1. Handrails are not required for ramped aisles with seating on both sides. 2. Handrails are not required where, at the side of the aisle, there is a guard with a top surface that complies with the grasp- ability requirements of handrails in accordance with Section 1014.4. 3. Handrail extensions are not required at the top and bottom of stepped aisles and ramped aisles to permit crossovers within the aisles.

quotes.text: 1030.17.1 Perimeter guards. Perimeter guards shall be provided where the footboards or walking surface of seating facilities are more than 30 inches (762 mm) above the floor or grade below. Where the seatboards are adjacent to the perimeter, guard height shall be 42 inches (1067 mm) high minimum, measured from the seatboard. Where the seats are self-rising, guard height shall be 42 inches (1067 mm) high minimum, measured from the floor surface. Where there is an aisle between the seating and the perim- eter, the guard height shall be measured in accordance with Section 1015.3. Exceptions: 1. Guards that impact sightlines shall be permitted to comply with Section 1030.17.3. 2. Bleachers, grandstands and folding and telescopic seating shall not be required to have perimeter guards where the seating is located adjacent to a wall and the space between the wall and the seating is less than 4 inches (102 mm).

quotes.text: 1010.1.1 Size of doors. The required capacity of each door opening shall be sufficient for the occupant load thereof and shall provide a minimum clear opening width of 32 inches (813 mm). The clear opening width of doorways with swinging doors shall be measured between the face of the door and the frame stop, with the door open 90 degrees (1.57 rad). Where this section requires a minimum clear opening width of 32 inches (813 mm) and a door opening includes two door leaves without a mullion, one leaf shall provide a minimum clear opening width of 32 inches (813 mm). In Group I-2, doors serving as means of egress doors where used for the movement of beds shall provide a minimum clear opening width of 41 1/2 inches (1054 mm). The minimum clear open- ing height of doors shall be not less than 80 inches (2032 mm).

The required capacity of each door opening shall be sufficient for the occupant load thereof and shall provide a minimum clear opening width of 32 inches (813 mm). The clear opening width of doorways with swinging doors shall be measured between the face of the door and the frame stop, with the door open 90 degrees (1.57 rad). Where this section requires a minimum clear opening width of 32 inches (813 mm) and a door opening includes two door leaves without a mullion, one leaf shall provide a minimum clear opening width of 32 inches (813 mm). In Group I-2, doors serving as means of egress doors where used for the movement of beds shall provide a minimum clear opening width of 41 1/2 inches (1054 mm). The minimum clear open- ing height of doors shall be not less than 80 inches (2032 mm).

lines.title: Egress · Space between two doors in a series, and their swings (BCNYS 1010.1.7): A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Two doors in a series (in a vestibule or anywhere else on the way out) are at least 48 inches apart plus the width of a door swinging into the space, and swing the same way or away from the space between them; horizontal sliding power-operated doors need only 48 inches, storm and screen doors serving Group R-2 and R-3 dwelling units need not be 48 inches from the other door (they still swing as above), and doors within those units, other than within Type A units, are excepted: doors in a series and the space between them aren't in the model, so a person's check.

lines.title: Egress · One motion to unlatch, no manual bolts (BCNYS 1010.2.1): A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Unlatching any door or leaf for egress takes no more than one motion in a single linear or rotational direction to release every latch and lock, and manual bolts aren't permitted; except in places of detention or restraint; manual bolts, automatic flush bolts and constant latching bolts on a pair's inactive leaf as 1010.2.4 item 4 and Table 1010.2.4 permit, that leaf without a doorknob, panic hardware or similar operating hardware; and a Group R dwelling or sleeping unit's single exit door (1006.2.1 or 1006.3.4) with a night latch, dead bolt, manual bolt or security chain that needs a second releasing motion, per 1010.2.4 item 5, each openable from the inside without a key or tool: hardware isn't in the model, so a person's check.

lines.title: Egress · Locks and latches that stop a door opening, where permitted (BCNYS 1010.2.4): A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A lock or latch may keep an egress door from opening only where one of 1010.2.4's ten items applies (or a locking system of 1010.2.9 to 1010.2.15, section group 6e), each with its own conditions: 1, places of detention or restraint; 2, Group I-1 Condition 2 and Group I-2 where the clinical needs of persons receiving care require containment or persons receiving care pose a security threat, all clinical staff able to readily unlock the doors at all times, the locks keyed to keys all clinical staff carry at all times or all clinical staff having the codes or other means at all times; 3, in Group A of 300 or fewer, Groups B, F, M and S and places of religious worship, the main exterior doors or the main doors to the tenant space with a key-operated lock from the egress side, readily distinguishable as locked, a readily visible durable sign on the egress side on or adjacent to the door ("THIS DOOR TO REMAIN UNLOCKED WHEN THIS SPACE IS OCCUPIED") in 1-inch letters on a contrasting background, its use revocable by the building official for due cause; 4, manual bolts, automatic flush bolts and constant latching bolts on a pair's inactive leaf per Table 1010.2.4, that leaf without a doorknob, panic hardware or similar operating hardware; 5, a Group R dwelling or sleeping unit's single exit door (1006.2.1 or 1006.3.4) with a night latch, dead bolt, manual bolt or security chain that needs a second releasing motion, openable from the inside without a key or tool; 6, fire doors after the minimum elevated temperature has disabled their unlatching per listed fire door test procedures; 7, doors serving roofs not intended to be occupied, locked against entry from the roof; 8, other than egress courts, exit access doors where occupants must egress from an exterior space through the building, with an approved locking device, the maximum occupant load posted where 1004.9 requires it (permanently, inside, conspicuously near every exit access doorway), a weatherproof telephone or two-way communication system (1009.8.1, 1009.8.2) beside at least one required exit access door on the exterior side, a key-operated lock readily distinguishable as locked, a clear window or glazed door opening of at least 5 sq ft at each exit access door, a readily visible durable sign on the interior side on or beside each locked door ("THIS DOOR TO REMAIN UNLOCKED WHEN THE OUTDOOR AREA IS OCCUPIED", letters at least 1 inch high on a contrasting background), and the exterior area's occupant load at most 300 (1004); 9, doors to balconies, decks or other exterior spaces serving a dwelling or sleeping unit; 10, doors to such spaces of 250 sq ft or less serving a private office: how each door locks isn't in the model, so a person's check.

lines.title: Egress · Bolts on the inactive leaf of a pair of doors (BCNYS Table 1010.2.4): A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Manual (surface- or flush-mounted) bolts, automatic flush bolts and constant latching bolts on a pair's inactive leaf only as Table 1010.2.4 permits, by use and whether the pair must comply with Section 716 (fire door assemblies, not brought in): Group B, F or S under 50 occupants, and Group B, F or S with a 903.3.1.1 sprinkler system where the inactive leaf isn't needed for egress capacity (a pair not under 716: all three; a 716 pair: constant latching bolts, and automatic flush bolts under note b); Group I-2 patient care and sleeping rooms, that leaf not needed (constant latching bolts, and automatic flush bolts under note b, whether or not under 716); any occupancy where panic hardware isn't required, the doors used in pairs and both leaves needed for egress capacity (automatic flush bolts only, under note b for a 716 pair); storage or equipment rooms, that leaf not needed (all three; note a: no manual bolts on Group I-2 corridor doors required to be positive latching). Note b: automatic flush bolts where both leaves are self-closing or automatic-closing with a coordinator that closes the inactive leaf before the active leaf. Which doors are pairs, their bolts and their fire rating aren't in the model, so a person's check.

lines.title: Egress · Interior stairway doors openable from both sides (BCNYS 1010.2.6): A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Interior stairway egress doors open from both sides without a key or special knowledge or effort; except a stairway's discharge door, openable from the egress side and locked only from the other; doors arranged per 403.5.3 (not brought in); stairway exit doors locked from the side opposite egress only where they open from the egress side and can be unlocked together without unlatching by all of these: individually or together on a signal from the fire command center, where present, or by emergency personnel from a single location inside the main entrance; together on a fire alarm signal when a fire alarm system is present in an area served by the stairway; and on failure of power to the electric lock or locking system; and stairway exit doors openable from the egress side and locked only from the other in Groups B, F, M and S where the only interior access to the tenant space is from a single exit stairway 1006.3.4 permits, and in Group R-2 where the only interior access to the dwelling unit is from such a stairway: how each door locks isn't in the model, so a person's check.

lines.title: Egress · Intruder locks in educational occupancies (BCNYS 1010.2.7): A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): In Group E, Group B educational and Group I-4 occupancies, egress doors from classrooms, offices and other occupied rooms with locks to keep intruders out can be unlocked from outside the room with a key or other approved means, open from within per 1010.2, and leave listed panic hardware, fire door hardware and door closers unmodified, fire door assemblies modified only per NFPA 80; remote locking or unlocking from an approved location is permitted too: locks aren't in the model, so a person's check.

lines.title: Egress · Panic hardware on electrical rooms' doors (BCNYS 1010.2.8.2): A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Exit or exit access doors serving transformer vaults, rooms for batteries or energy storage systems, or modular data centers have panic or fire exit hardware; and where a room holds electrical equipment rated 800 amperes or more with overcurrent, switching or control devices and its door is less than 25 feet from the working space NFPA 70 requires, the door has no latch or lock other than panic or fire exit hardware and swings in the direction of egress travel: which rooms hold such equipment isn't in the model, so a person's check.

lines.title: Egress · Where delayed egress locks are permitted (BCNYS 1010.2.12): A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Delayed egress locks are permitted only in buildings sprinklered throughout per 903.3.1.1 or with an approved automatic smoke or heat detection system per 907, and only for Groups B, F, I, M, R, S and U, Group E classrooms of under 50, and courtrooms in Groups A-3 and B on doors other than the main exit or exit access door (there sprinklered throughout per 903.3.1.1): delayed egress locks aren't in the model, so a person's check.

DOOR CAN BE OPENED IN 15 [30] SECONDS, meeting ICC A117.1's visual characters (not required where approved in Group I care areas that need restraint or containment); emergency lighting is on the egress side; and the locking device is listed to UL 294 or UL 1034: delayed egress locks aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Enclosed areas with walls and ceilings in buildings or structures with open-air assembly seating are protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system per 903.3.1.1; but not the floor area used for contests, performances or entertainment where the roof construction is more than 50 feet above the floor and the use is restricted to low fire hazard uses, press boxes and storage facilities under 1,000 square feet, or open-air seating facilities whose seating and means of egress in the seating area are essentially open to the outside: whether seating is open-air isn't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where one of the two paths of travel crosses the aisle through a row of seats to another aisle, there are at most 24 seats between the two aisles, and the row between them is at least 12 inches clear plus 0.6 inch for each seat above seven; for smoke-protected or open-air seating, at most 40 seats, and 12 inches plus 0.3 inch for each additional seat: seats and rows aren't drawn, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Every occupied portion of a building, room or space used for assembly purposes that contains seats, tables, displays, similar fixtures or equipment has aisles leading to exits or exit access doorways as 1030 requires (1030.1: a room or space used for assembly purposes containing seats, tables, displays, equipment or other material complies with 1030): aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An aisle's clear width is at least: 48 inches for stepped aisles with seating on both sides, or 36 inches where they serve fewer than 50 seats; 36 inches for stepped aisles with seating on one side only, or 23 inches between a stepped aisle handrail and the seating where the aisle serves no more than five rows on one side; 23 inches between a stepped aisle handrail or guard and the seating where a mid-aisle handrail divides the stepped aisle; 42 inches for level or ramped aisles with seating on both sides, or 36 inches where they serve fewer than 50 seats, or 30 inches where they serve fewer than 15 seats and aren't part of an accessible route; 36 inches for level or ramped aisles with seating on one side only, or 30 inches where they serve fewer than 15 seats and aren't part of an accessible route: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An aisle has capacity enough for the people in the catchment area it serves, the portion of the whole space that section of the aisle serves, worked out assuming a balanced use of all the means of egress, the number of people in proportion to egress capacity: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where aisles converge into a single path of egress travel, that path's required capacity is at least the combined required capacity of the converging aisles: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The portions of aisles where egress is possible in either of two directions are uniform in minimum width or required capacity: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Each end of an aisle continues to a cross aisle, foyer, doorway, vomitory, concourse or stairway per 1030.9.7 with access to an exit; but a dead-end aisle may be up to 20 feet long; longer where the seats beyond its first 20 feet are at most 24 seats from another aisle, along a row at least 12 inches clear plus 0.6 inch for each seat above seven where the seats have backrests, or beyond 10 where they don't; one serving fewer than 50 seats and complying with 1030.8; and for smoke-protected or open-air seating, dead-end vertical aisles of 21 rows or fewer, or longer where the rows beyond are at most 40 seats from another aisle, along an aisle accessway at least 12 inches clear plus 0.3 inch for each seat above seven where the seats have backrests, or beyond 10 where they don't: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An aisle's clear width is measured to walls, edges of seating and tread edges, but for permitted projections; an aisle beside seating at tables may be measured per 1030.13.1 instead: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Nothing obstructs an aisle's minimum width or required capacity; but handrails may project into the required width of stepped and ramped aisles per 1014.9: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A stairway connecting a stepped aisle to a cross aisle or concourse may meet 1030.14's assembly aisle walking surface requirements, and the transitions between such stairways and stepped aisles comply with 1030.10: stepped aisles and their stairways aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A stairway connecting a vomitory to a cross aisle or concourse may meet 1030.14's assembly aisle walking surface requirements, and the transitions between such stairways and stepped aisles comply with 1030.10: vomitories and their stairways aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A transition between a stairway and a stepped aisle meets 1030.10.1 or 1030.10.2: where the stepped aisles, transitions and stairways keep the stepped aisle's riser and tread dimensions, they comply with 1030.14 as one exit access component: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where a stairway and a stepped aisle with different riser and tread dimensions meet (1030.10.2 to 1030.10.3) in a straight run, the transition is at least 22 inches deep where the treads on its descending side are deeper, or at least 30 inches where they are shallower: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where the stairway changes direction from the stepped aisle, the transition between them is at least 11 inches deep, or the stepped aisle's tread depth if that is more: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A distinctive marking stripe at least 1 inch and at most 2 inches wide is at each nosing or leading edge next to the transition, distinctly different from the stepped aisle's contrasting marking stripe: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where a stepped aisle changes direction at a vomitory (1030.11), its treads there are at least 11 inches deep, or the stepped aisle's tread depth if that is more, and a tread's height above a transition at a vomitory complies with 1030.14.2.2: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A transition between the stepped aisle above a vomitory and the stepped aisles beside it is at least 11 inches deep, or the stepped aisle's tread depth if that is more: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Aisles, stepped aisles and ramped aisles are built of materials consistent with the types permitted for the building's type of construction; wood handrails are permitted in every type: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The surface of aisles, stepped aisles and ramped aisles is of slip-resistant materials, securely attached, and a stepped aisle's surface complies with 1011.7.1: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Outdoor aisles, stepped aisles and ramped aisles, and the outdoor approaches to them, are designed so that water doesn't accumulate on the walking surface: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Aisle accessways serve seating at tables per 1030.13.1 and seating in rows per 1030.13.2: where seating at a table or counter is next to an aisle or aisle accessway, its required clear width is measured to a line 19 inches from and parallel to the table's or counter's edge, measured perpendicular to that side; other side boundaries are measured to walls, edges of seating and tread edges; where fixed seats serve the tables or counters, the width is measured from the back of the seat: tables and seats aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An aisle accessway serving seating at tables or counters meets 1005.1's capacity and is at least 12 inches wide plus 1/2 inch for each additional foot, or part of one, beyond 12 feet of its length measured from the center of the seat farthest from an aisle; but a portion at most 6 feet long and used by at most four people in all is exempt: tables and seats aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Travel along an aisle accessway at tables is at most 30 feet from any seat to the point where a person has a choice of two or more paths of egress travel to separate exits: tables and seats aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where rows have 14 or fewer seats, the aisle accessway between them is at least 12 inches clear, measured horizontally from the back of the row ahead to the nearest projection of the row behind: with automatic or self-rising seats raised, any other seat down, and folding tablet arms in use (or stored, where a tablet arm raised to vertical in one motion falls back to stored by gravity): seats and rows aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A row of seating served by aisles or doorways at both ends has at most 100 seats, and the 12 inches between rows grows by 0.3 inch for every seat beyond 14 where the seats have backrests, or beyond 21 where they don't, to at most 22 inches needed; for smoke-protected or open-air seating, Table 1030.13.2.1 gives the row lengths a 12-inch aisle accessway may serve before it widens: seats and rows aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The most seats a row of smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating may have with a 12-inch clear aisle accessway, by the total number of seats (with backrests and without, an aisle or doorway at both ends, then at one end only): fewer than 4,000, 14, 21, 7 and 10; 4,000 to 6,999, 15, 22, 7 and 10; 7,000 to 9,999, 16, 23, 8 and 11; 10,000 to 12,999, 17, 24, 8 and 11; 13,000 to 15,999, 18, 25, 9 and 12; 16,000 to 18,999, 19, 26, 9 and 12; 19,000 to 21,999, 20, 27, 10 and 13; 22,000 and more, 21, 28, 11 and 14: seats and rows aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): For a row served by an aisle or doorway at one end only, the 12 inches between rows grows by 0.6 inch for every seat beyond seven where the seats have backrests, or beyond 10 where they don't, to at most 22 inches needed; for smoke-protected or open-air seating, Table 1030.13.2.1 gives the row lengths a 12-inch aisle accessway may serve before it widens: seats and rows aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Ramped aisles comply with 1030.14.1 to 1030.14.1.3 and stepped aisles with 1030.14.2 to 1030.14.2.4: an aisle sloped more than 1 in 20 (5 percent) is a ramped aisle; one that is part of an accessible route per 1009 and 1109.2 is at most 1 in 12 (8 percent), and any other at most 1 in 8 (12.5 percent): aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A ramped aisle's slope measured perpendicular to the direction of travel is not steeper than 1 in 48 (2 percent): aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Ramped aisles have landings per 1012.6 to 1012.6.5, which may overlap required aisles or cross aisles: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Ramped aisles have edge protection per 1012.10 and 1012.10.1; but in assembly spaces with fixed seating, not on the sides where the ramped aisle gives access to the adjacent seating and aisle accessways: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An aisle sloped more than 1 in 8 (12.5 percent) is a series of risers and treads across its full width, complying with 1030.14.2.1 to 1030.14.2.4: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Stepped aisle treads are at least 11 inches deep and uniform, adjacent treads differing by at most 3/16 inch: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where a stepped aisle's gradient matches the adjoining seating's, its risers are at least 4 and at most 8 inches high and uniform within each flight; but they may vary only as far as the seating's changing gradient needs for sightlines, each variation over 3/16 inch between adjacent risers marked by a distinctive stripe 1 to 2 inches wide on each tread at the nosing next to it, distinct from the contrasting marking stripe; and risers up to 9 inches are permitted where the adjacent seating's slope needs them for sightlines: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Adjacent risers designed equal differ by at most 3/16 inch; where the stepped aisle takes 1030.14.2.2's exception 1, each riser of unequal height differs from the adjacent ones, in the direction of descent, by at most 3/8 inch where its treads are less than 22 inches deep, and by at most 3/4 inch where they are 22 inches or more: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Each tread has a contrasting marking stripe at least 1 inch and at most 2 inches wide at its nosing or leading edge, so each tread is readily seen in descent; but it may be left out where the tread surfaces already make each tread readily apparent in descent: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.
A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A stepped aisle's nosing and riser profile comply with 1011.5.5 to 1011.5.5.3: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): In a building, room or space used for assembly purposes, seats are securely fastened to the floor; but not where there are no ramped or tiered floors for seating and 200 or fewer seats, nor at tables without ramped or tiered floors; over 200 seats without ramped or tiered floors, they are fastened together in groups of at least three or fastened to the floor; where flexible seating is integral to a space on tiered levels, up to 200 seats need not be fastened (plans showing seating, tiers and aisles submitted for approval); nor groups of at most 14 seats on level floors set apart by railings, guards, partial height walls or similar barriers; nor seats for musicians or other performers set apart so: seats aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Ramped aisles sloped more than 1 in 15 (6.7 percent) and stepped aisles have handrails per 1014, at one or both sides or within the aisle width; a stepped aisle with seating on one side and 74 inches wide or more has two, one within 30 inches horizontally of the side of the tiered floor next to it; but no handrails are needed on ramped aisles with seating on both sides, nor where a guard at the aisle's side has a top as graspable as a handrail per 1014.4, and no extensions at the top and bottom where they would block crossovers: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where there is seating on both sides of the aisle, or a stepped aisle needs two handrails, mid-aisle handrails are discontinuous, with gaps or breaks at most every five rows, each at least 22 and at most 36 inches clear, measured horizontally, and the handrail ends rounded or bent: aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Handrails at the side of stepped aisles return to a wall, guard or the walking surface, or continue to the handrail of the next stepped aisle flight: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Mid-aisle handrails don't extend beyond the lowest riser and end within 18 inches of it, measured horizontally, with no extensions needed; but they may extend beyond it where their extensions don't obstruct the cross aisle's width: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where stepped aisles have mid-aisle handrails, an additional rail is about 12 inches below the handrail, its strength and attachment per 1607.9.1.2: stepped aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Guards next to seating in a building, room or space used for assembly purposes are provided where 1015 requires them and built per 1015, except as 1030.17.1 to 1030.17.4 provide; at bleachers, grandstands and folding and telescopic seating, guards are provided where ICC 300 and 1030.17.1 require them: guards and seating aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Perimeter guards are provided where the footboards or walking surface of seating are more than 30 inches above the floor or grade below: at least 42 inches high measured from the seatboard where seatboards adjoin the perimeter, or from the floor where seats are self-rising, and measured per 1015.3 where an aisle lies between the seating and the perimeter; but guards that impact sightlines may meet 1030.17.3, and bleachers, grandstands and folding and telescopic seating need none where the seating is next to a wall less than 4 inches away: guards and seating aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Cross aisles more than 30 inches above the floor or grade below have guards per 1015; where the drop between a cross aisle and the floor or grade below is 30 inches or less, guards at least 26 inches above the aisle floor; but none where the backs of the seats at the front of the cross aisle rise 24 inches or more above the aisle's floor: guards and cross aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Unless 1030.17.4 applies, a fascia or railing system meeting 1015's guard requirements and at least 26 inches high is provided where the floor or footboard is more than 30 inches above the floor or grade below and the fascia or railing would otherwise interfere with the sightlines of the seating right beside it: guards and seating aren't in the model, so a person's check.

A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where the foot of an aisle is more than 30 inches above the floor or grade below, a fascia or railing system meeting 1015's guard requirements runs the aisle's full width, at least 36 inches high and giving at least 42 inches measured diagonally between the top of the rail and the nosing of the nearest tread: guards and aisles aren't in the model, so a person's check.
